title: Emotions Create Habits
coreMove: Engineer a genuine feeling of success in the seconds after a tiny behavior ends, so the brain wires repetition by feeling rather than willpower

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice nurse trying to build a thirty-second decompression habit between patient rooms
exampleSpecs.audience: a night-shift hospice nurse running on empty
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she can keep showing up emotionally for dying patients without burning out by month's end
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she finishes one slow exhale in the hallway and quietly says 'good' to herself, and notices the moment land in her chest before she opens the next door

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school orchestra teacher learning to praise himself the way he praises his students
exampleSpecs.audience: a mid-career music teacher who feels silly celebrating his own actions
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether his new habit of writing one sentence of his overdue dissertation each morning survives past the second week
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: his coach pushes back when he says 'celebration feels cheesy,' and he tries a quiet 'nailed it' after closing his laptop and feels something he wasn't expecting

exampleSpecs.domain: a long-haul trucker designing a stretch he can do at fuel stops without feeling ridiculous in front of other drivers
exampleSpecs.audience: a fifty-three-year-old trucker with chronic lower back pain
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether he keeps his commercial license through his next physical exam
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after one shoulder roll at the pump, he taps the side of the truck twice and grins to himself, and the small private grin is the entire wiring

exampleSpecs.domain: a recently widowed retiree teaching herself to celebrate making the bed each morning
exampleSpecs.audience: a sixty-eight-year-old woman whose mornings have lost their shape
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the day starts with one small win or with the weight of the empty house
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before the celebration she finishes the bed and feels nothing; after she adds a hand placed on the smoothed quilt and a soft 'there,' she notices the day has a foothold

exampleSpecs.domain: a junior pastry cook practicing celebration during an unrelenting Saturday brunch service
exampleSpecs.audience: a twenty-three-year-old line cook who thinks any visible joy at work looks unprofessional
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she can build a habit of plating one dessert with full attention before the shift swallows her
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she imagines two parallel versions of the same plated tart, one finished with a flat exhale and one finished with a private internal 'yes,' and traces which version of her shows up to plate the next ticket

exampleSpecs.domain: a software contractor whose celebration of writing one test felt fake until he stopped performing it
exampleSpecs.audience: a remote contractor who tried celebration for a week and quit
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether he resurrects a habit-building method he's already publicly written off
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: looking back at his abandoned attempt, he realizes he was performing a celebration he didn't feel, and identifies the exact moment a real micro-flicker of pride would have been available if he'd stayed honest

exampleSpecs.domain: a parent of a colicky four-month-old learning to celebrate finishing one diaper change without checking her phone
exampleSpecs.audience: a sleep-deprived new parent at 3 a.m.
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one anchor of presence survives a season she'll barely remember
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she catches the small warm feeling of having been fully there for sixty seconds, names it as the glue, and lets it count without scaling it up into anything more
